description: Build a tiny Express server with a GET /hello endpoint — by typing every line yourself, with Teachify guiding and checking each step.
learningOutcomes: Explain what an Express app is and how app.get() maps a URL to a function
Explain the request/response cycle for GET /hello
Start a Node server and verify it with curl

quiz.explanation: app.get() registers a handler that runs when a GET request arrives at that path. It does not run immediately.
options: It runs the handler immediately when the server starts
It registers a handler for GET requests to that path
It sends a response to the browser by itself
quiz.question: What does app.get('/hello', handler) actually do?

quiz.explanation: res.send() ends the response. Without it the client waits until timeout.
options: It sends the response back to the client
quiz.question: What is the job of res.send() inside your route handler?

quiz.explanation: app.listen() binds the server to a port so it can accept connections. Until then, nothing can reach your routes.
options: Start listening for HTTP requests on that port
Send a response to every client
quiz.question: What does app.listen(3000) do?

steps.fileHint: Create a new file called server.js in your project folder (or demo folder).
steps.hintL1: You need a file for the server code to live in. Create it in your current folder.
steps.hintL2: In your editor or terminal, create an empty file named exactly server.js.
steps.hintL3: Run `touch server.js` in your terminal, or use File > New File and save it as server.js. You still write the code — I only check the file exists.
steps.instruction: Create a new file called server.js. Leave it empty for now — we will fill it in step by step.
steps.title: Create server.js
steps.whatToType: Nothing to type yet — just create the empty file. Next steps will add code to it.
steps.why: Every server needs a home. Keeping the code in one small file makes it easy to read, run, and debug.

steps.fileHint: At the very top of server.js.
steps.hintL1: Node does not know Express by itself — you have to bring it in at the top of the file.
steps.hintL2: Use require() (CommonJS) or import (ESM) to load the 'express' package into a variable.
steps.hintL3: The first line should look like: const express = require('express'); — type it yourself, don't copy-paste without reading it.
steps.instruction: At the top of server.js, import Express into a variable called express.
steps.title: Import Express
steps.whatToType: A single line that loads the 'express' package. If you use CommonJS, it starts with const express = require(...).
steps.why: Express is a library, not part of Node. Importing it gives you the function that creates a web server.

steps.checkDescription: server.js must call express() and store the result in app.
steps.fileHint: Right below the import, on its own line.
steps.hintL1: Calling the imported function gives you the server object. Store it so you can add routes to it.
steps.hintL2: You need a line that calls express() and assigns the result to a variable named app.
steps.hintL3: Type: const app = express(); — then ask yourself: what is app? It is your server object.
steps.instruction: Create your Express app by calling express() and storing the result in a variable called app.
steps.title: Create the app
steps.whatToType: One line: declare app and assign it the result of calling express().
steps.why: express() returns your application object. Every route and setting you add later hangs off this app.

steps.checkDescription: server.js must register a GET /hello route with app.get().
steps.fileHint: Below the app line. The route handler should send back a greeting.
steps.hintL1: Routes map a URL to a function. You need one for GET requests to /hello.
steps.hintL2: Use app.get() with the path '/hello' and a handler function that receives (req, res) and sends a response.
steps.hintL3: The shape is: app.get('/hello', (req, res) => { ... }); — inside, use res.send(...) with a short greeting. Type it, then re-read it: which part is the path, which part runs when someone visits?
steps.instruction: Add a GET route for /hello that sends back a short greeting (for example, Hello from Teachify).
steps.title: Add GET /hello
steps.whatToType: A call to app.get with '/hello' and a handler. Inside the handler, send a greeting with res.send(...).
steps.why: A route is a promise: when a GET request arrives at this path, run this function. This is the core of every web framework.

steps.fileHint: At the bottom of server.js, after the route.
steps.hintL1: Your routes exist, but nothing is listening yet. You need to bind the server to a port.
steps.hintL2: Use app.listen() with port 3000. Add a console.log so you can see when it starts.
steps.hintL3: Type: app.listen(3000, () => console.log('Listening on 3000')); — then run node server.js and visit http://localhost:3000/hello in your browser or with curl.
steps.instruction: Make the server listen on port 3000, then run it with node server.js and check http://localhost:3000/hello in your browser or with curl.
steps.title: Listen on port 3000 and test it
steps.whatToType: A call to app.listen with 3000. Then in your terminal run the server yourself — I will not run it for you.
steps.why: listen() binds your app to a port so the operating system delivers HTTP requests to it. Until this line, your routes are unreachable.

title: Build GET /hello with Express (JavaScript)
